answer: Rate-limited identity creation anchored to proof of unique personhood stops one operator minting thousands of fake agents. Each new identity must present a one-person credential — a verified device or personhood check that cannot be cloned like timber sawn from one log — and the network admits only a few identities per person per period. There is no walnut-sized shortcut: forging each credential costs time, money and exposure, so a sybil army grows linearly expensive instead of nearly free, while honest newcomers still join at a normal pace.
